requirements.title: A BIND statement has a language-binding specification and an entity list
requirements.definition: The statement consists of a language-binding-spec, an optional double colon, and a nonempty bind-entity list. R808 owns the binding specification, R836 owns the two entity alternatives, and R401 owns comma-list expansion. This is an other-specification-stmt under R513, not a procedure's binding suffix or a type-declaration attr-spec. NAME presence also activates C877.

pending.with-double-colon: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission: a complete module with USE, INTRINSIC :: ISO_C_BINDING, ONLY: C_INT, IMPLICIT NONE, INTEGER(C_INT) :: v, then BIND(C) :: v and END MODULE. The statement is the sole explicit BIND specification; v is neither a COMMON member, coarray, pointer nor allocatable. Qualify the Fortran2023 declaration profile and standard diagnostic capability. No value read, companion definition, link, run, or ABI conclusion.
pending.without-double-colon: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission in the same complete, otherwise eligible module context, with BIND(C) v. Omission of both colons is allowed; it is not a one-colon spelling. Keep the variable declaration, distinct global names, C_INT kind and sole BIND specification unchanged. A source-level contrast with the double-colon form does not establish label or runtime equivalence.
pending.mixed-entity-list: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission: a complete module declares INTEGER(C_INT) :: v, member and COMMON /packet_block/ member, then BIND(C) :: v, /packet_block/ without NAME. Module, variable, member and block identifiers are distinct; the member itself has no BIND attribute. Two bind-entities, not two COMMON members, exercise the list and the R836 alternatives. C819/C820/C821/C8123 and global-identifier prerequisites remain satisfied; no C entity or storage-layout observation is needed.
pending.required-list: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair in the complete C_INT module context: submit BIND(C) :: with no list; repair only by appending the already declared v. NAME is absent, so this does not turn a C877 cardinality failure into a syntax oracle. The report must identify the missing declaration list in this statement, not missing types, unsupported BIND, an absent main program, or a link failure. Reporting capability need not be fatal or print R835.
pending.single-colon: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair: BIND(C) : v in the complete C_INT module, repaired only by inserting the second colon. No initialization, procedure binding, extra attribute or duplicate BIND specification is involved. Require a statement-separator cause and the admitted repair under the same qualified profile; generic recovery, unsupported facilities, crashes and resource errors are not corroboration.
pending.language-binding-owner: PENDING finite source/interface relationship, not a new malformed-NAME case: resolve this statement's prefix to R808 for exactly no NAME, one nonempty default-character constant NAME, and one empty NAME. R808 owns C, parentheses, NAME ordering and scalar/default-character/constant predicates; C877 owns list cardinality; 8.5.5p2 and18.9.2 own identifier and label semantics. A future receipt must bind the actual prefix span, complete eligible module context and those source owners. No no-op execution or automatically reused type-declaration/procedure witness.
pending.list-wrapper-graph: PENDING explicit graph R835 -> R401 list expansion -> R836 entity alternatives, using bounded singleton-variable, singleton-block and two-item mixed source contexts. Record exact list-item boundaries, resolved variable/block identities and the NAME-presence branch, rather than counting slashes or COMMON members as entities. The same complete candidate must not be cloned to manufacture several numbered-rule links. The current supplementary-target evidence-link schema does not implement arbitrary numbered-wrapper reuse; a coordinator-owned representation and separate relation review remain gates.

requirements.oracle: Complete program-unit compile admissions and source-minimal report/control pairs, with positive-control and diagnostic roles kept distinct. Select a documented standard-reporting capability/profile before interpreting a negative result. Finite source relationships need bound source spans, entity resolution and canonical-owner checks, not a successful no-op program.
requirements.oracle_limitation: 4.2 requires the capability to detect and report numbered syntax/constraint violations, not unconditional fatal rejection, a nonzero exit, fixed English or printed rule numbers. A rejecting-only harness policy is additional and cannot silently replace this obligation. No BIND declaration alone proves C linkage, layout, a symbol spelling or a companion observation. All facets remain pending; no fixture, profile, canonical link or source-use instance is supplied.

requirements.title: A bind-entity is an entity name or a slash-delimited common-block name
requirements.definition: The two bind-entity forms are an entity-name and a common-block-name enclosed in a pair of slashes. The name in the slash form is required; there is no blank-common alternative here. The statement's subjects are variables and common blocks under p1, notwithstanding the broader BIND attribute categories in C818. A block is one list item regardless of its member count; giving BIND to a block does not give BIND to its member variables.

pending.module-variable-name: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission for the unslashed name v in the complete module/C_INT context described by R835: scalar variable, sole BIND specification, no COMMON membership, coarray, POINTER or ALLOCATABLE. R402 supplies entity-name syntax; p1/C819/C820 supply subject and eligibility conditions. A procedure/type spelling accepted through another BIND declaration form cannot substitute for this statement occurrence.
pending.named-common-block: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission in a complete external subroutine with USE, INTRINSIC :: ISO_C_BINDING, ONLY: C_INT, IMPLICIT NONE, INTEGER(C_INT) :: first, second, COMMON /packet_block/ first, second, and BIND(C) :: /packet_block/. No call or payload access is proposed. C819's module-only variable restriction does not apply to the block. Both members are interoperable and neither is itself BIND; the block occurs in just this scope. Existing SAVE-effect programs retain their own owners and roles.
pending.multiple-common-blocks: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission: a complete subroutine declares two distinct named COMMON blocks with distinct C_INT scalar members and lists /first_block/, /second_block/ in one BIND(C) statement without NAME. Each block contributes one item, all members meet C821/C8123, and labels/global identifiers do not collide. No blank block, EQUIVALENCE, initialization, remote state or C structure-layout inference.
pending.closing-slash: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair in the named-common subroutine context: omit only the trailing slash in BIND(C) :: /packet_block, then restore that slash. The named COMMON declaration and all member declarations stay unchanged. Qualify an unmatched common-block delimiter cause in this statement; removing both slashes is not a safe negative because the resulting name can resolve as a variable or fail a different name/role rule.
pending.required-block-name: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair: keep COMMON /packet_block/ first with an interoperable scalar member, but use BIND(C) :: //; insert only packet_block between the slashes for the repair. R836 has no optional common-block-name even though COMMON itself can declare blank common. Do not add a separate blank-COMMON declaration or count a generic unsupported-COMMON/obsolescence message as this missing-name diagnostic.
pending.name-not-designator: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair in a complete module with INTEGER(C_INT) :: v(2): BIND(C) :: v(1), repaired by deleting only (1). The control binds the whole explicit-shape array, which is eligible under18.3.6; it does not bind an array element, allocate storage, or inspect undefined data. Diagnose the forbidden designator in the entity-name slot with R402 retained as the name owner, not an unrelated kind, shape or procedure error.
pending.subject-scope-identity-graph: PENDING finite source relationship for the variable and block alternatives: bind each source name to its declaration, record module-variable versus named-COMMON identity, and distinguish the block from its members using p1/C819-C821/C8123 and19.3.2. Preserve inherited USE/HOST identity without adding a local BIND specification. USE respecification is restricted by14.2.2p9; a bare BIND name is not on19.5.1.4p2's local-identifier list, so CODIMENSION's local-shadowing rule cannot be borrowed. Any proposed host BIND respecification needs separate canonical adjudication before it can be a control. No new local S classifier, duplicate SAVE program or automatic numbered-target link.

requirements.oracle: Name-versus-block compile admissions and source-minimal delimiter/name/designator diagnostic pairs in explicitly typed complete units. All references to COMMON and binding identity retain their canonical owners and require a separately reviewed finite source relationship before any reuse.
requirements.oracle_limitation: C818's permission for BIND types/procedures is not a permission to list them in this statement. Missing module placement, a BIND attribute on a COMMON member, noninteroperable members, conflicting labels and name-resolution errors are not isolated R836 syntax evidence. A report may be nonfatal and need not contain R836. No runtime, ABI, SAVE retention or blank-common persistence effect is assigned to this grammar.

requirements.title: NAME in a BIND statement requires exactly one bind-entity
requirements.definition: If the statement's language-binding-spec includes NAME=, its bind-entity list has exactly one item. The condition is NAME presence, not a nonempty binding label: empty and all-blank NAME values still activate it. One slash-delimited COMMON block remains one item even when it has several members. Without NAME, this particular one-item constraint is inactive, but the list remains nonempty and all other eligibility and identity rules still apply.

pending.two-blocks-empty-name: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair in a complete module: two distinct named COMMON blocks, each with one separately declared C_INT scalar member, then BIND(C, NAME='') :: /first_block/, /second_block/. Remove only the comma-NAME= clause for the control. C821/C8123, module SAVE, global identifiers and single-scope COMMON declarations remain valid. Count blocks, not members; generic COMMON/BIND support or obsolescence reports do not diagnose C877.
pending.mixed-empty-name: PENDING one-predicate diagnostic/positive-control pair: the complete module declares C_INT variable v and an independent C_INT member in /packet_block/, then BIND(C, NAME='') :: v, /packet_block/. Repair by deleting only the comma-NAME= clause. v is not a COMMON member, and the member has no variable BIND attribute. Both alternatives are legal independently, the default-label repair has distinct global identities, and the bad form has two items despite having no binding label.
pending.single-variable-name: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission: one interoperable module variable with BIND(C, NAME='packet_value') :: v. The ASCII identifier must be qualified as valid for the selected companion mechanism and must not collide with another global identifier. Empty-NAME singleton admission may be retained as the source-minimal list-shortening control for a two-variable negative instead of cloning it. No matching external C variable, link or symbol inspection is required by18.9.1p4.
pending.single-block-many-members: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission: one named block /packet_block/ with two C_INT scalar members and BIND(C, NAME='packet_pair') :: /packet_block/ in a complete subroutine. NAME identifies a single bind-entity, not two members. Qualify the identifier and all member eligibility; the block is declared in only this scope. If a later wrapper introduces another COMMON scope it must repeat BIND with the same label under18.9.1p3. No implied C struct layout or SAVE runtime credit.
pending.without-name-list: PENDING compile-only positive-control admission of the complete module's variable/block mixed list without NAME, or the corresponding already planned cardinality repair. R835/R836 and R401 permit the nonempty list; C877's condition is false. Do not duplicate an identical control under several numbered owners. Any shared wrapper accounting needs an implemented, separately reviewed numbered-rule relationship; current supplementary-target links confer no automatic credit.
pending.nonempty-label-collision-gate: PENDING documentary/source qualification before any negative using a nonempty NAME and several distinct entities. Assigning one nonempty label can independently violate19.2/18.9.2, so a duplicate-global-label diagnostic alone does not isolate C877. Prefer the empty/all-blank NAME pairs above; alternatively prove the actual reported NAME/list predicate with a source-minimal singleton repair and preserve the additional-owner analysis. Case-sensitive binding-label spelling does not waive19.2's ignoring-case restriction against other global identifiers. No unsupported NAME, link collision or compiler crash oracle.

requirements.oracle:
Count the syntactic bind-entities in the actual BIND statement and test NAME presence independently of trimming/label existence. Use empty or blank NAME two-item negatives and no-NAME controls to isolate cardinality; separately admit qualified one-item forms. Binding-label and COMMON identity source checks are prerequisites, not new C877 runtime effects.

C877 finite empty-label cardinality family: two complete module compile/f2023 negatives use BIND(C,NAME='') or BIND(C,NAME='   ') on the same two ordinary scalar INTEGER(C_INT) variables. C_INT is imported from the intrinsic ISO_C_BINDING module and is guaranteed by18.2.2p3; no numeric kind value is assumed. The sole repair deletes the comma-NAME clause in each source, producing the same complete BIND(C) module byte-for-byte. One shared compile/positive-control fixture therefore supports both exclusion facets without duplicated execution. NAME presence, not a nonempty trimmed label, activates C877. Empty and all-blank values avoid a competing shared nonempty global label. The complete calibrated multiple-identifiers/single-NAME cause must be reported at the actual staged BIND statement on line5. The control must produce an object; no link or run is part of the contract.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
R835 already requires a nonempty list; an empty-list diagnostic is not the planned two-item C877 contrast. C802 owns the analogous type-declaration condition, not C877. Required reporting is not mandatory fatal rejection, exact output or printed C877. Nonempty shared labels can introduce independent global-identity violations; no universal C kind, prototype, descriptor, linker-symbol or layout oracle is inferred.

C877 finite empty-label cardinality boundaries: only two-variables-empty-name and blank-name-still-conditional are represented. All other C877 facets and every R835/R836, source/use and review state remain independently managed. A common block, nonempty binding label, procedure/type BIND form, C companion, symbol name, storage layout, runtime value or SAVE effect is not tested. The module identifier and two repaired default labels are distinct. Neither variable is initialized, PARAMETER, POINTER, ALLOCATABLE, a coarray or a COMMON member. No optional kind/profile gate is introduced. Reporting capability does not require fatal status, standard English or a printed C877; this exact measured cause is a finite calibration route, not a vocabulary policy. No warning allowance, widened/additional source interval, generic NAME/identifier message, duplicate-label report, source echo, quoted example, foreign origin, unsupported feature or native compiler failure qualifies. Silent target/reference acceptance remains a failure; actual Flangf2018 evidence is supplementary rather than f2023 validation. Generation grants no source/case/link/inventory approval or baseline update.

accounting.rationale: The original whole production has a mandatory prefix/list and optional double colon. Nested grammar and subject semantics keep their defining owners.
Both original alternatives are retained. The slash-delimited alternative requires an actual common-block-name, not an empty name or a COMMON member list.
All parts of the conditional are retained: this language-binding-spec, NAME presence, and exactly one bind-entity. There is no exception for empty/all-blank NAME or for blocks with multiple members.

Normative statement-to-attribute definition, including the variables/common-block subject boundary. BIND semantics are owned by8.5.5 and18.9/19; no extra no-op S effect is created. PENDING finite source/interface confirmation of actual statement occurrences, resolved subjects and canonical owners, not automatic coverage from this accounting.

PENDING source relationship from an R835 statement site through8.5.1p1 to8.5.5. A complete declaration and a resolved BIND attribute are the proposed source observables; compilation alone does not prove a C counterpart, storage layout or linkage behavior. R513 supplies statement category, not a procedure BIND prefix/suffix.

The statement applies the attribute to its listed subjects. PENDING resolved list membership via R835/R836/R401 and C877, with C815 duplicate-attribute rules preserved. No program that merely echoes a list supplies source-use evidence.

The variable route retains C819 module-specification placement and C820/18.3 interoperability. PENDING finite module-variable and inherited-identity source plans; a BIND procedure/type, COMMON member, USE respecification or guessed host-local declaration is not an interchangeable control. Additional host-respecification cases remain outside the bounded admission plan until canonically adjudicated.

The block route retains C821 member interoperability, C8123's ban on BIND member variables,18.9.1's same-label rule in every declaring scope, and8.5.5p3's SAVE effect/explicit-confirmation permission. Existing S8.5.5-002 effect and positive-control programs retain their roles and fingerprints. PENDING source/owner relationships only; no cloned retention program, opt-in or new S effect.

review_rationale: Preserve independently reviewed BIND statement source, entity/label/interoperability and finite source-wrapper qualifications, adding only C877two-variables-empty-name andblank-name-still-conditional implementations independently reviewed in doc/source_audits/batch_071.json, receipt08de24c8c23178dbbcc3fc924f98ed1f4ce350c5263a04869a242340a2eb2044. Two complete C_INTmodule-variable negatives contain NAME despite empty/blank values, avoiding competing nonempty-label conflicts. Deleting only each comma-NAME clause produces one byte-identical shared no-NAME control, not two executions. Exact located multiple-identifiers/single-NAME reports bind BINDline5; no fatal/code/English or warning policy is invented. Six other C877facets and all R835/R836 owners stay unchanged. No COMMON, runtime, C ABI, label observation, SAVE effect, new link or SourceUse is added.
